note: Sample cosmos for the My Universe first slice. Every place and value is a fictional world; nothing here is real astronomy.

galaxies.name: Lyra Spiral
galaxies.summary: A barred spiral with bright violet arms and one charted star system.

galaxies.name: Aurora Elliptical
galaxies.summary: An old, golden elliptical galaxy. No systems charted here yet.

systems.name: Lyra Prime
systems.summary: A single yellow star with three charted planets.

planets.name: Thalassa
planets.summary: A warm ocean world with volcanic headlands and long, steady swells.

facts.text: Almost the whole surface is ocean; a few volcanic headlands break the water.
Swells are long and regular, driven by steady trade winds.
A research platform floats off the largest headland.

planets.name: Ignis
planets.summary: A dark basalt world crossed by glowing fissures. One fissure field is charted for landing.

facts.text: Columnar basalt plains cover most of the surface.
Days are hot and hazy; the sky glows copper near the horizon.

planets.name: Boreas
planets.summary: A ringed ice giant. No landing site is charted yet.

facts.text: Its rings are mostly ice and dust.

planets.requirementText: Sample requirement: an Ice and Climate mission reviewed by your coach.

environments.name: Thalassa Research Station
environments.summary: A bounded stretch of open ocean beside a basalt headland, with a floating research platform.

locations.name: Research platform
locations.purpose: Future home of a floating-settlement design project.
observations: Platform deck about 40 m across (fictional world value).

locations.name: Tide gauge
observations: Tidal range about 1.8 m (fictional world value).

locations.name: Weather mast
locations.purpose: Measures wind, temperature and pressure on the headland.
observations: Steady easterly wind, about 6 m/s (fictional world value).

locations.name: Vent overlook
locations.purpose: A shallow hydrothermal vent visible through clear water.
observations: Warm water shimmers above the vent (illustrative, not simulated).

environments.name: Ignis Fissure Field
environments.biome: Basalt plain, lava fissure and columnar terrace
environments.summary: A charted stretch of basalt plain where a glowing fissure runs past a terrace of six-sided columns, with a gas vent and an automated sensor station.

locations.name: Sensor station
locations.purpose: An automated station that logs gas, temperature and ground tremors.
observations: Air temperature at the station about 41 °C (fictional world value).
A future atmospheric chemistry workstation could be based here.

locations.name: Glowing fissure
locations.purpose: An open crack where molten rock glows below a thin crust.
observations: Crust beside the crack about 1 m thick (fictional world value).
The glow is illustrative, not a simulation of lava or heat flow.

locations.name: Basalt columns
locations.purpose: A terrace of six-sided rock columns that formed as thick lava cooled and cracked.
observations: Columns about 1.5–2 m across (fictional world value).

locations.name: Gas vent
locations.purpose: A vent releasing sulfur-rich gas into the hazy air.
observations: The plume shown is illustrative, not simulated.
A possible future site for an SO₂ → sulfate chemistry investigation.
